event: On Day 19 Wren wakes in camp to the threshold stone's signature humming in the ground.
The insect chorus is still silent; the ghost-elms hum looser, unclenched after the pulse.
Forty meters south, [Foundation Stone] runs as a low vibration in the base of her spine.
She dresses and goes south to the stone.
The thirty-second dawn vibration comes back, full and uninterrupted.
The stone says hello, and she had not known how much she needed to hear it.
The cloud broke overnight; the healer's south window faces the dawn as it was built to.
Her margin column counts down from Day 4 to Day 18 and zero, where it became a hinge.
Below the zero she writes 'Day 19. One.', a count from what happened, not toward it.
Walking the perimeter, she feels the signature as a heartbeat in every foundation.
The ghost-elm shimmer is greener; the ward reaches a few centimeters further than before.
She lets the settlement settle around her and does not reach for discoveries.
She finds Theron in the drainage channel, clearing silt with a flat stone as a trowel.
He has worked since dawn; under the silt the lining is intact. 'Water will move.'
A lining stone warms under her thumb with the [Foundation Stone] signature.
'You didn't ask. You just started.' 'Yes,' Theron says, and goes back to clearing.
She sees she paid little attention to the person beside her for eighteen days; she files it.
'Can I help?' 'You can survey. Tell me if the gradient changes at the south bend.'
The six-degree gradient holds the whole length; she tells him, and he nods.
They work in parallel for an hour in companionable silence.
She sees the settlement gaining new daily acts of care, layered on the healer's old ones.
The thought of the Hearth slot sits at the edge of her awareness, unfollowed.
After midday she goes to the gap: the same size, its settlement edge now a sharp line.
Her hand on the dead tree feels nothing; the gap neither grows nor shrinks.
She writes: 'The gap is not a wound anymore. It is a scar.' She lets it stand.
In the afternoon she sits against the stone to spend her three Level 5 points.
PER is thirteen with the class bonus: seeing is what she does.
ATT is fourteen, her highest: the capacity to hold a connection open.
EMP is eleven with [Tended]; she thinks of Theron, Maret, Hadley and Brecca.
She puts +1 into PER, because she is a Wayfinder and seeing is what she does.

changes.note: Level 5 free point allocated to PER

event: She puts +1 into EMP, because the next thing that matters is people.

changes.note: Level 5 free point allocated to EMP

event: She puts +1 into ADP, the stat the stone gave her: endurance is a thing you are.

changes.note: Level 5 free point allocated to ADP

event: She notices she put nothing into ATT: she needs what makes connection worth having.
Theron comes back to the fire in late afternoon, mud on his forearms, satisfied.
'The south bend is clear. Water will flow to the tree line.' 'Good drainage,' she says.
Fourteen families lived here; they built the drainage first, before walls or hall.
Then the forest changed, they left, silt filled the channel, and the walls held anyway.
'And now you're clearing the silt.' 'I'm clearing the silt,' he agrees.
She does not ask if he is staying; they drink tea in the evening light.
Journaling, she notices she treated his work as landscape, not conversation.
She logs the day's notes and adds: 'Theron is clearing the little river.'
In her bedroll she hears the insect chorus returning in ones and twos.
The ten links rest; the stone's signature is the steadiest signal among them.
The Eye still watches south-southeast, toward Hearthstone, where she has never been.
She reckons Hadley, gone since Day 15, back by Day 21 or 22, Brecca perhaps behind him.
She sees 'the count says five' may have been unkind: she sent Brecca a stat screen.
She keeps the thought she does not like. Day 19. One.
On Day 20, mid-morning, she is at the threshold stone when she hears Hadley coming.
Hadley comes into the clearing, mud-booted, talking to himself, carrying two packs.
'Mail.' He hands her a letter from her mother; she tucks it unread into her journal.
Aldric sends regards; her father sends nothing, thinking too hard to write it down.
'And Brecca Vane sends a question.' She got the message and said: 'Five what?'
Brecca was half-packed at Aldric's counter when he left; he did not advise her.
'If she left the morning after I did, she'll be here tomorrow. Day after at the latest.'
Wren is used to not knowing things about places, not about people.
'What should I have said?' 'I found something important and I want to show it to you.'
'You're good at places, Wren. People are a different survey.' He is right.
She writes 'Day 20. Two.' and that people are a different survey.
Hand on the humming stone, she thinks of what she meant and what she said; the count climbs.
